strategy.title: Product strategy for SkillSetu
strategy.summary: SkillSetu wins tier-2 first-job seekers by making 10-minute speaking practice feel like interview prep, not an English class. In one year it proves people will pay by moving from 2% to 5% paid conversion on Android, offline-friendly, before raising a seed round.

sections.content: Within a year, a graduate in Nagpur or Indore can walk into their first job interview and answer in confident spoken English, after practising 10 minutes a day on a ₹199 phone app instead of a ₹4,000 coaching course (Assumption: typical coaching fee).

- **Retention:** 18% D7 retention means most users stop before speaking improves enough to notice.
- **Willingness to pay:** only 2% pay today; users compare us with free YouTube and Duolingo.
- **Patchy 4G and cheap phones:** speech feedback that needs a fast connection fails exactly for our users.
- **No speech AI team:** we must build on third-party speech APIs, which cost money per minute.

By the end of 1 year:
- 5% of active users pay for the ₹199 plan (from 2%).
- D7 retention of 30% (from 18%).
- 3,000 paying users (Assumption), enough to show a repeatable paid funnel to seed investors.

MVP with 6k sign-ups from a pilot, 18% D7 retention and 2% paid conversion. Team of 4 with ₹15 lakh runway, so roughly 12 months (Assumption: about ₹1.2 lakh monthly burn). Users mostly come from word of mouth in 2 pilot colleges (Assumption).

1. **Practice tied to the interview, not grammar.** Every lesson is an interview question they will face, which beats Duolingo's general English for this user and is the reason to pay.
2. **Works on bad networks.** Lessons and feedback that degrade gracefully offline, which coaching apps built for metros do not do.
3. **Prove payment before scale.** We choose conversion and retention over sign-up growth; we will not spend on paid installs this year.

- **Mock interview streaks** (intent 1): a daily 10-minute mock round with one scored answer; expected to lift D7 retention to 30% (Assumption).
- **Offline lesson packs** (intent 2): download a week of lessons on Wi-Fi; speaking is recorded offline and scored when back online.
- **'Interview in 30 days' paid plan** (intent 3): a clear outcome promise with a free first week; expected to move conversion from 2% to 5%.
- **College placement-cell pilots** (intent 3): 3 colleges where placement officers recommend the plan, to test a cheaper acquisition channel.

- **North Star:** weekly users who complete 3+ speaking practices (Assumption: target 4,000 by month 12).
- Paid conversion: 2% to 5%.
- D7 retention: 18% to 30%.
- Speech API cost per paying user under ₹40 a month (Assumption), so the ₹199 plan stays profitable.

assumptions: Users will pay for an interview outcome more than for general English. Test: two pricing pages in the pilot colleges.
Offline recording with delayed scoring is good enough. Test: 2-week beta with 200 users on low-end phones.
Placement officers will recommend us. Test: pitch to 5 colleges and count sign-ups per college.

sections.content: Weekly users who complete 3 or more speaking practices, target 4,000 in 12 months (Assumption). It measures the value users get: actually speaking, not just opening the app.

- **Ravi, 22, BCom graduate in Indore:** we promise he can answer 'Tell me about yourself' fluently in 30 days.
- **Pooja, 21, final-year student in Nagpur:** we promise practice that works on her patchy 4G.

- Daily mock interview streaks to lift D7 retention from 18% to 30%.
- Offline lesson packs for low-end phones, and also a web version, a tutor marketplace, group classes and a corporate plan for employers.
- A paid 'Interview in 30 days' plan to move conversion from 2% to 5%.

- Practices started per user per week (input) drives weekly active speakers (output).
- Offline pack downloads (input) drives practices on bad networks.
- Free-week to paid conversion (input) drives revenue.
